question: For delivered order items, how many more days on average does delivery take when the seller is in a different state from the customer than when they are in the same state? Use fractional days from purchase to customer delivery.
sql:
WITH delivery_times AS (
    SELECT
        CASE WHEN c.customer_state = s.seller_state THEN 'same' ELSE 'different' END AS state_relation,
        EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (o.order_delivered_customer_date - o.order_purchase_timestamp)) / 86400.0 AS delivery_days
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
    JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN sellers s ON oi.seller_id = s.seller_id
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
      AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
    AVG(CASE WHEN state_relation = 'different' THEN delivery_days END) -
    AVG(CASE WHEN state_relation = 'same' THEN delivery_days END) AS avg_day_difference
FROM delivery_times
